q: What does a yellow (amber) light mean?
a: The red light is about to appear: stop if you can do so safely; otherwise go with caution
w: Speed up to get through before it turns red
Stop immediately, even if you're in the intersection
The light is broken: treat it as an all-way stop
e: Yellow = red is coming. Stop if it's safe to stop.
s: A yellow - or amber - light means the red light is about to appear. You must stop if you can do so safely; otherwise, go with caution.

q: The green light ahead of you is flashing. What does it mean?
a: Advance green: you may turn left, go straight or turn right; oncoming traffic still has a red
w: The light is about to turn red
Proceed with caution; it's a broken light
e: A flashing green is an advance green. Oncoming traffic is still stopped.
s: This is called an advanced green light because oncoming traffic still faces a red light.

q: A left-turn green arrow is shown with a red light. What does it mean?
a: You may turn left from the left-turn lane; oncoming left-turners may be turning too
w: You may go straight or turn left
Turn left only after stopping completely
e: Simultaneous left turn: left-turners from both directions go together.
s: When a left-turn green arrow is shown with a red light, you may turn left from the left-turn lane.

q: This round signal on top of the traffic light shows a white vertical bar. What does it mean?
a: Transit priority signal: traffic and pedestrians must yield to public transit vehicles
w: The light is out of order
e: The white bar lets buses or streetcars go while all conflicting traffic faces red.
s: Traffic and pedestrians must yield to public transit vehicles at a transit priority signal.

q: The traffic lights are completely dark because of a power failure. What does that mean?
a: Treat the intersection like an all-way stop
w: The main road keeps the right-of-way
e: Dead lights = all-way stop. Yield to vehicles in the intersection and to vehicles coming from your right.
s: Go cautiously and use the intersection the same way you would use an intersection with all-way stop signs.

q: The yellow light ahead is flashing. What does it mean?
a: Drive with caution as you approach and go through the intersection
w: The light is about to turn red
e: Flashing yellow = caution. Flashing red = stop.
s: A flashing yellow light means you should drive with caution when approaching and moving through the intersection.

q: A single flashing yellow beacon hangs above an intersection. What does it mean?
a: Drive with caution
w: Yield to traffic from the left
e: A flashing yellow beacon warns you to drive with caution.
s: A flashing yellow beacon above an intersection, above a warning sign or on an obstruction in the road, warns you to drive with caution.

q: Which signal shows a green light with a left-pointing green arrow (an advance green)?
a: lights/3-2-5.jpg
e: A green arrow together with a green light = advance green.
s: When you face a flashing green light or a left-pointing green arrow and a green light, you may turn left, go straight ahead or turn right from the proper lane.

q: Which signal means: don't start your left turn, the green light is about to appear for other traffic?
a: lights/3-2-7.jpg
e: The yellow arrow (with a red light) comes after the green arrow.
s: After the left-turn green arrow, a yellow arrow may appear. This means the green light is about to appear for traffic in one or both directions.

q: Which signal shows a fully protected left turn with a green arrow?
a: lights/3-2-10.jpg
e: Fully protected left turns have their own separate signal, marked "left turn signal".
s: You may turn left from the left-turn lane when you face a green arrow.

q: At an intersection with a separate left-turn signal, which picture shows yellow for left-turning vehicles only?
a: lights/3-2-11.jpg
e: After the left-turn green arrow, a yellow light appears for left-turners only.
s: After the left-turn green arrow, a yellow light appears for left-turning vehicles only.

q: Which picture shows a red light for left-turning vehicles only, while other traffic has a green light?
a: lights/3-2-12.jpg
e: Fully protected left turn: red for left-turners while straight and right-turning traffic go.
s: After the yellow light, a red light appears for left-turning vehicles only.

q: Which is a flashing red beacon?
a: lights/3-2-16.jpg
e: A beacon is a single flashing light. Red beacon = complete stop.
s: A flashing red beacon above an intersection or stop sign means you must come to a complete stop.

q: Which picture shows a transit priority signal?
a: lights/3-2-9.jpg
e: The extra round signal on top shows a white vertical bar for transit vehicles.
s: The round signal is on top of a regular traffic signal and shows a white vertical bar on a dark background.

q: Which picture shows traffic lights that are out because of a power failure?
a: lights/3-2-15.jpg
e: All the lights are dark. Use the intersection like an all-way stop.
s: During an electrical power loss, traffic lights at intersections will not work.

q: Flashing green light vs regular green light: what's special about the flashing green?
a: Oncoming traffic still faces a red light, so you may turn left without waiting for them
w: Nothing; they mean exactly the same
It means the light is about to turn yellow
It means pedestrians have the right-of-way
e: Flashing green = advance green. On a regular green, left-turners must yield to oncoming traffic.
s: This is called an advanced green light because oncoming traffic still faces a red light.

q: You face a green light with a left green arrow. What may you do?
a: Turn left, go straight or turn right from the proper lane
w: Turn left only after oncoming traffic clears
e: Green arrow + green light = advance green, the same as a flashing green.
s: you may turn left, go straight ahead or turn right from the proper lane

q: You face a left green arrow with a RED light. You want to go straight. What do you do?
a: Wait: only left turns from the left-turn lane may go
w: Go straight, since the arrow is green
Turn left instead, from any lane
e: The red light still applies to through traffic. The arrow is only for left turns.
s: When a left-turn green arrow is shown with a red light, you may turn left from the left-turn lane.

q: A yellow arrow appears after the green arrow. What does it mean?
a: The green is about to appear for other traffic: don't start your turn; stop if you can safely
w: Left turns are allowed until the light turns red
e: Yellow arrow = your turning time is ending.
s: Do not start your left turn. Stop if you can do so safely; otherwise, complete your turn with caution.

q: The red light ahead is flashing. What must you do?
a: Come to a complete stop, then go when it's safe
w: Slow down and go with caution
Stop and wait for it to turn green
Yield only to vehicles on your right
e: Flashing red = treat it like a stop sign.
s: You must come to a complete stop at a flashing red light. Move through the intersection only when it is safe.

q: Flashing yellow vs flashing red: which statement is right for a flashing YELLOW light?
a: Drive with caution; you don't have to stop
w: Treat it as an all-way stop
e: Flashing red = stop. Flashing yellow = caution.
s: A flashing yellow light means you should drive with caution when approaching and moving through the intersection.

q: A single flashing red beacon hangs above a stop sign. What does it mean?
a: Come to a complete stop; go only when it's safe
w: Slow down and go with caution
e: Red beacon = complete stop, just like the stop sign.
s: A flashing red beacon above an intersection or stop sign means you must come to a complete stop. Move through the intersection only when it is safe to do so.

q: A flashing yellow beacon is placed over a warning sign. What does it tell you?
a: Drive with caution
w: The sign is no longer in effect
Speed up to clear the hazard
e: Yellow beacons warn; red beacons stop.
s: A flashing yellow beacon above an intersection, above a warning sign or on an obstruction in the road, warns you to drive with caution.

q: The left green arrow has ended and the light is now a solid green. Can you still turn left?
a: Yes, but only when the way is clear of traffic and pedestrians
w: No, left turns are only allowed on the arrow
Yes, oncoming traffic must stop for you
Only if you were first in line
e: On a plain green, you may turn left after yielding.
s: You can still turn left when the light is green, but only when the way is clear of traffic and pedestrians.

q: At a fully protected left turn, the left-turn signal shows red but straight-ahead traffic has green. Can you turn left?
a: No: you may not begin a left turn after the green light appears for other traffic
w: Yes, if no oncoming traffic is coming
Yes, but only on a one-way road
e: At these intersections, left turns go only on the left-turn arrow.
s: In these intersections, you may not begin turning left after the green light appears for traffic going straight ahead or turning right.

q: What is a traffic beacon?
a: A single flashing light hung over an intersection, or placed over signs or on obstacles in the road
w: A light on top of a police car
A traffic light with an arrow
e: Beacons are single flashing lights: red = stop, yellow = caution.
s: A traffic beacon is a single flashing light hung over an intersection or placed over signs or on obstacles in the road.

q: What does a transit priority signal look like?
a: A round signal on top of a regular traffic light, showing a white vertical bar
e: The white vertical bar is for buses and streetcars.
s: The round signal is on top of a regular traffic signal and shows a white vertical bar on a dark background.

q: Which light colour is also called "amber"?
a: Yellow
e: Yellow and amber mean the same light.
s: A yellow - or amber - light means the red light is about to appear.

q: Where can a flashing yellow beacon be placed?
a: Above an intersection, above a warning sign, or on an obstruction in the road
e: Yellow beacons warn you to drive with caution.
s: A flashing yellow beacon above an intersection, above a warning sign or on an obstruction in the road, warns you to drive with caution.

q: You have a green light and want to turn left. What must you do?
a: Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians, then turn when it's clear
w: Turn right away; green means you have the right-of-way
Turn left before the oncoming cars move
e: Green lets you go after yielding to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection.
s: A green light means you may turn left, go straight or turn right after yielding to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection.

q: You have a green light and are turning right. A pedestrian is crossing the road you're turning onto. What must you do?
a: Yield to the pedestrian
w: Turn quickly before they reach your lane
e: When turning on a green light, pedestrians crossing the intersection have the right-of-way.
s: When turning left or right you must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians crossing the intersection.

q: The light turns yellow and you are close enough to stop safely. What should you do?
a: Stop
w: Speed up to make it through
Keep your speed and go through
e: Stop on yellow if you can do it safely.
s: You must stop if you can do so safely

q: The light turns yellow when you are so close that you can't stop safely. What should you do?
a: Drive through the intersection with caution
w: Back up behind the stop line
Stop in the middle of the intersection
e: If you're too close to stop safely, go through with caution.
s: However, if you are already so close that you cannot stop safely, drive through the intersection with caution.

q: You're at a red light and want to turn right. There's no sign forbidding it. What must you do?
a: Come to a complete stop, wait until the way is clear, then turn
w: Slow down and turn if clear
Turn without stopping if no pedestrians are near
e: Right on red is allowed after a full stop, unless a sign says no.
s: Unless a sign tells you not to, you may turn right on a red light only after coming to a complete stop and waiting until the way is clear.

q: When may you turn LEFT on a red light?
a: From a one-way road onto a one-way road, after a complete stop
w: From any road, after a complete stop
Only when a police officer waves you on
e: Left on red only works one-way to one-way.
s: You may also turn left on a red light if you are moving from a one-way road onto a one-way road, but you must come to a complete stop first and wait until the way is clear.

q: You must stop for a red light. There is a stop line painted on the road. Where do you stop?
a: At the stop line
w: At the edge of the intersection
At the crosswalk on the far side
e: Stop line first. No line: crosswalk. No crosswalk: edge of the sidewalk. No sidewalk: edge of the intersection.
s: Bring your vehicle to a complete stop at the stop line if it is marked on the pavement.

q: You come to a flashing red light. What must you do?
a: Stop completely, then go when it's safe
w: Wait for the light to turn green
Stop only if traffic is coming
e: A flashing red light works like a stop sign.
s: You must come to a complete stop at a flashing red light.

q: The traffic lights are out. You and a car on your right arrive at the same time. Who goes first?
a: The car on your right
w: Whoever is on the busier road
e: Dead lights = all-way stop. Yield to vehicles in the intersection and entering from your right.
s: Yield the right-of-way to vehicles in the intersection and to vehicles entering the intersection from your right.

q: You're in the middle of a fully protected left turn when the left-turn signal turns yellow. What should you do?
a: Complete your turn with caution
w: Back up to the stop line
Wait for the next green arrow
e: If it turns yellow while you're already in the intersection, finish the turn with caution.
s: If the light turns yellow while you are in the intersection, complete your turn with caution.

q: You're turning left on a green light and the light turns red while you're in the intersection. What should you do?
a: Complete your turn when it's safe
e: Don't stay stuck in the intersection. Finish the turn when it's safe.
s: If the light turns red when you are in the intersection, complete your turn when it is safe.

q: The transit signal shows a white vertical bar. A bus beside you wants to go. What do you do?
a: Yield to the bus: the signal is for transit vehicles
w: Turn right in front of the bus
Honk to let the bus know you're there
e: At a transit priority signal, everyone else yields to transit vehicles.
s: This allows transit vehicles to go through, turn right or left, while all conflicting traffic faces a red light.

q: The light is flashing green. A pedestrian is waiting to cross in front of you, but there's no pedestrian signal. May they cross?
a: No: pedestrians must not cross on a flashing green unless a pedestrian signal tells them to
w: Yes, pedestrians may always cross on green
Yes, if they push the button
Only if a crossing guard is there
e: Flashing green is for turning traffic; pedestrians wait.
s: Pedestrians must not cross on a flashing green light unless a pedestrian signal tells them to.
